comments.content:
This sample runs under the `runtime-runes` suite, whose `common_setup` always passes `runes: true` to the compiler (`packages/svelte/tests/runtime-legacy/shared.ts`, line 161, applied after `...config.compileOptions`). With an explicit `runes: true`, `analyze_component` computes `runes = true` and the new `maybe_runes` fallback added in this PR is never reached (`maybe_runes` requires `!runes` and `options.runes === undefined`). The component would therefore be compiled in runes mode anyway and these assertions (`p` becomes `1`) would pass even with the compiler change reverted, so this test provides no regression coverage for the `export const` case.

To actually cover the fallback the component must be compiled without an explicit `runes` option (the harness currently forces it, so a config/suite that leaves it undefined is needed). It would also be worth asserting `p?.innerHTML === '0'` before the click, so the test proves reactivity after the update instead of only proving the initial render.
